    Lantana camara is the most studied invasive in Indian dry deciduous forests — by far. The literature corpus + OpenAlex surfaced 15+ relevant papers. Key findings that apply to EBTL:
    
    - **Prasad (2011, J. Tropical Ecology)** — Lantana-native plant relationships in southern Indian deciduous forest — found Lantana cover correlates with reduced native diversity at landscape scale
    - **Wilson et al. (2013, J. Tropical Ecology) — Lantana's effect on elephant habitat use in Mudumalai** — directly relevant since EBTL is in the same dry-deccan elephant corridor
    - **Ramaswami & Sukumar (2013, PLoS ONE)** — long-term correlates of Lantana invasion in seasonally dry tropical forest — canopy gaps and disturbance drive invasion
    - Hiremath & Sundaram (2005) — the fire-Lantana cycle: Lantana promotes fire, fire opens canopy, Lantana spreads faster
    - **Kannan et al. (2016, Forest Ecology & Management) — local use (harvesting for baskets/fuel) can suppress Lantana** in southern Indian forests — management-relevant finding for community engagement
    - **Lone et al. (2022, Biotropica)** — Lantana alters soil nitrogen pools AND flora in dry deciduous forest
    - **Bhagwat et al. (2012, PLoS ONE)** — two centuries of Lantana management across India/Australia/SA — notes manual removal alone is rarely enough
